concept: A key the reader presses, drawn as a small keycap lit from above, the same raised slab as every surface in Pane.

default_to_avoid.pattern: a grey monospace box with a 1px border (GitHub kbd, the browser kbd)
default_to_avoid.why_not: a bordered grey box owns a colour and a border Pane does not use; monospace reads as code

derivation.consequence: light falls from above, so every surface carries a rim brightest along its top edge and a soft shadow below that says where it floats, and a recess is the inverse, shaded under its top lip and lit on its bottom lip; a nested surface adds no second blur, because one sheet of glass is one layer
derivation.form: a keycap is a raised slab lit at its top with a short soft shadow under it

derivation.consequence: the rim and sheen are white at low opacity, like light catching an edge
derivation.form: its rim and sheen are white at low opacity, the same light as every surface

derivation.consequence: secondary text keeps the lowest opacity that still measured as passing; text halos count only where WCAG allows them
derivation.form: the key is printed in the caption size of the interface face, not monospace

variants.reason: A is a small Pane slab, lit from above (P3). B brings a border and a grey. C cannot be told apart from emphasis.

root.why: a small raised slab lit at its top with a short shadow, printed with the key in the caption size

@media forced-colors: active.why: forced colours draw an outline so the key keeps its shape
